name: Artemas
overview: Artemas is a male figure mentioned in the New Testament, specifically in Titus 3:12. He is noted for possibly being sent by the Apostle Paul to assist Titus in his ministry. Beyond this potential mission, Scripture provides no further details about his tribe or additional background.
namesAndTitles: The name Artemas appears as a proper name in the New Testament without any specified meaning or divine origin. The Bible simply identifies him by this name without further explanation of its significance.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record any family relationships for Artemas beyond what is indicated in his possible association with Paul and Titus. There are no other relational details provided in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Artemas holds significance as a trusted companion or helper whom Paul considered sending to Titus, indicating his role in supporting early church leadership and ministry. His mention reflects the cooperative efforts among early Christian workers to strengthen local churches. Although briefly noted, Artemas represents the faithful individuals who contributed to the spread of the gospel through service and partnership.
